subject.title: fix(security): add default pidsLimit for sandbox containers

question: Should OpenClaw make `1024` the default Docker sandbox `pidsLimit` for existing configs, or keep unlimited-by-default behavior and route PID hardening through an explicit opt-in or doctor/docs path?
rationale: The source confirms the security gap, but changing a sandbox resource default can break existing workloads and the current schema blocks the documented zero opt-out, so automation should not choose the product/security boundary.

options.title: Require compatibility-ready default
options.body: Proceed with a default pids cap only after the PR aligns schema/docs/tests, proves opt-out behavior, and supplies real Docker proof for fresh and existing containers.

options.title: Prefer opt-in hardening
options.body: Keep the current runtime default and add a documented/doctor-visible hardening path for operators who want process limits without surprising existing workloads.

options.title: Pause for security redesign
options.body: Hold this PR and use the open security issue to decide whether PID limits, `--init`, ulimits, or another sandbox-control strategy should be canonical.

recommendation.title: Require compatibility-ready default
recommendation.body: Proceed with a default pids cap only after the PR aligns schema/docs/tests, proves opt-out behavior, and supplies real Docker proof for fresh and existing containers.
